title: SIRUI Unveils the Swift Series: Compact, All-Glass Full-Frame Autofocus Lenses
summary: SIRUI unveils Swift series of ultra-compact, full-frame autofocus lenses for creators
detailed: SIRUI has announced the launch of its new Swift series, a lineup of ultra-compact, full frame autofocus lenses tailored for photographers and content creators seeking lightweight glass without sacrificing optical integrity.
SIRUI Swift 20mm f/2.4 : Delivers an ultra-wide 91.5° diagonal field of view.
SIRUI is launching both Swift lenses in Sony E and L-mount versions, with Fujifilm X-mount versions also listed on its official store.

Both the Swift 20mm f/2.4 and Swift 40mm f/2.2 are priced at $149 each, making the series an exceptionally accessible entry point for creators building out a lightweight primary kit or a streamlined secondary setup.
sentences: SIRUI has announced the launch of its new Swift series, a lineup of ultra-compact, full frame autofocus lenses tailored for photographers and content creators seeking lightweight glass without sacrificing optical integrity.
This launch offers two lenses: a 20mm f/2.4 and a 40mm f/2.2.
With both lenses weighing in at roughly 210 g each, SIRUI did not choose to lean toward using plastic optical elements.

In fact, they achieve the lightweight setup by intentionally avoiding overly complex designs and using all-glass optical construction as the core foundation of the Swift lineup to keep them remarkably small.

Despite their compact form factor, both options feature integrated manual aperture rings, nine-blade circular apertures for smooth out-of-focus transitions, and STM autofocus motors designed to handle quiet, responsive tracking for both stills and video workflows.
To keep filter management simple across a dual-lens kit, both models share a standard 58mm front filter thread.
SIRUI Swift 20mm f/2.4 : Delivers an ultra-wide 91.5° diagonal field of view.
SIRUI Swift 40mm f/2.2 : Provides a natural, everyday perspective.
SIRUI is launching both Swift lenses in Sony E and L-mount versions, with Fujifilm X-mount versions also listed on its official store.
Additional mount options are planned, although Nikon Z availability has not been confirmed.

Both the Swift 20mm f/2.4 and Swift 40mm f/2.2 are priced at $149 each, making the series an exceptionally accessible entry point for creators building out a lightweight primary kit or a streamlined secondary setup.
